title: How Ancient Physicians Separated a Seizure From a God — Babylonian Sakikku Semiology, Hippocratic On the Sacred Disease, Jacksonian Cortical March, Berger's EEG & SCN1A Interneurons

teenKit.tldr: For millennia, humans blamed sudden, invisible brain seizures on vengeful gods and demons because bones left no clues. This episode tracks our epic 3,000-year journey from clay tablets to modern genetics to decode the brain's electrical storms.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding seizures transformed how society treats medical conditions, proving that terrifying, mysterious body spasms are physical wiring glitches rather than supernatural curses.
keyTakeaways: Ancient Mesopotamian doctors carefully cataloged seizure symptoms on clay tablets called the Sakikku, trying to spot patterns before they understood electricity.
The Greek text 'On the Sacred Disease' was a massive historical turning point, arguing that seizures are physical diseases of the brain, not divine possessions.
Modern science bridged the gap from macro-behavior to micro-genetics, using tools like EEGs and discovering misfiring protein molecules like SCN1A.

vocab.meaning: An ancient Babylonian diagnostic handbook written on clay tablets that detailed medical symptoms and prognoses.
A wave-like progression of a seizure moving step-by-step across the brain's motor cortex, causing spasms to march down a patient's body.
A medical test invented by Hans Berger that uses sensors on the scalp to record the electrical activity of the brain.
A specific genetic channel protein that helps regulate nerve cell firing, whose mutation can trigger severe epileptic seizures.

quiz.question: Why did ancient people originally attribute sudden seizures to gods or demons?
options: Because religious leaders forced them to believe it.
Because the human skull and skeleton showed no visible physical damage or marks after death.
Because they had microscopes that showed tiny spirits.
Because seizures only happened during religious ceremonies.
quiz.explanation: With pristine bones and zero tools to see electricity or brain chemistry, people filled the invisible biological void with supernatural explanations.

quiz.question: What was the core revolutionary argument of the Hippocratic text 'On the Sacred Disease'?
options: That seizures were caused by angry gods living in the clouds.
That seizures had a natural physical origin rooted in the brain.
That only priests could cure epilepsy with special rituals.
That seizures were completely harmless and required no treatment.
quiz.explanation: The text famously argued that epilepsy is no more 'divine' than any other disease, boldly shifting humanity toward natural medical science.

quiz.question: How did Hans Berger fundamentally change the study of epilepsy in the 20th century?
options: By translating ancient Babylonian clay tablets into Greek.
By inventing brain surgery to remove damaged tissue.
By creating the first rudimentary brainwave recordings (EEG) to visualize electrical activity.
By discovering the DNA sequence for the SCN1A gene.
quiz.explanation: Berger's invention of the EEG allowed scientists to finally see the invisible brain storms by tracking electrical waves on paper.
